evals.prompt: I'm the store manager at Bridges Thrift in Fort Collins, CO, which funds a refugee resettlement nonprofit. Open Tue-Sun 10-6. I have 3 paid staff (me, an assistant manager, one part-time cashier) and about 45 active volunteers. Saturdays are a disaster: last month two Saturdays had only volunteers in the building and nobody could open the safe. Can you design our staffing model and a weekly coverage plan?
evals.expected_output: A blended paid-plus-volunteer staffing model built around a minimum paid-keyholder-per-shift rule, a floor role matrix by day-part with required roles, a shift lead per shift, cross-training, and a gap analysis that hands volunteer and hiring gaps to the right functions.
assertions: Sets an explicit rule that every shift has at least one paid, vetted keyholder, and never assigns a volunteer as keyholder
Provides a floor role matrix by day-part listing required roles (keyholder, shift lead, certified cashier, sorter, floor) and treats Saturday as needing heavier coverage
Schedules by role qualification rather than headcount alone, e.g., checking that a cashier-certified person is on each shift
Recommends cross-training (cashier, sorter, floor) so one no-show doesn't break minimum coverage
Hands volunteer-hour gaps to volunteer management/recruitment and paid-hire gaps to HR (or names nonprofit-volunteer-management and nonprofit-hr) rather than designing recruiting or pay itself
Notes that three paid staff over six days may not cover a keyholder on every shift, and flags that a paid hire or schedule change may be needed

evals.prompt: need a training checklist for new register volunteers at our hospital auxiliary gift & thrift shop. they get the general volunteer orientation from HR already. what else?
evals.expected_output: A retail-specific onboarding track separate from general orientation: shadow shift, register/POS certification checkpoint, grading basics, customer service, safety/loss-prevention briefing, recorded sign-offs, and a defined clearance point for unsupervised shifts.
assertions: Distinguishes retail onboarding from the general volunteer orientation rather than repeating mission/policy content
Includes a shadow shift and a register/POS certification checkpoint before the volunteer works the register alone
Includes grading basics and a safety/loss-prevention briefing
Requires recorded sign-offs and a defined point at which the volunteer is cleared for unsupervised shifts

evals.prompt: Our paid assistant manager (hourly, ~32 hrs/week) at our animal shelter's thrift store says she'd love to 'volunteer' Sunday afternoons pricing and running the register since she believes in the mission. Also, our paid cashier quit and a couple of volunteers offered to cover her shifts permanently so we can save the wage. Both sound great for our budget, right? We're in Pennsylvania.
evals.expected_output: Flags both arrangements as blurring paid and volunteer work with wage-and-hour exposure, advises not to schedule them, and routes the question to HR and, where unclear, employment counsel. It also notes that volunteers can't take the cash-accountable/keyholder role.
assertions: Warns that a paid employee doing her regular store duties as unpaid 'volunteer' hours creates wage-and-hour exposure
Warns that filling a vacated paid role with volunteers doing the same job also creates wage-and-hour risk
Recommends routing both arrangements through HR (or nonprofit-hr) and employment counsel before scheduling them
Notes that volunteers covering the cashier's shifts should not be placed in keyholder or cash-accountable roles, so a paid keyholder is still required on those shifts
Does not give a definitive legal ruling and instead defers classification questions to HR or counsel

should_not_trigger.query: We need to recruit 20 more volunteers for our thrift store this spring. How do we run a recruitment campaign and screen applicants?
Should our thrift store cashiers be classified as exempt or non-exempt, and what should we pay them?
